lead.t: A common antecedent is duct obstruction by stones (sialolithiasis), but it can also be caused by impacted food debris or injury-related oedema.

snip.t: A common antecedent is duct obstruction by stones (sialolithiasis), but it can also be caused by impacted food debris or injury-related oedema.
Salivary duct stones (sialolithiasis): commoner in the submandibular gland (about 80%, because of its long, uphill duct and viscous mucus) than the parotid.

qs.q: An elderly, debilitated patient with dehydration and a history of recurrent sialolithiasis presents with an acutely painful and swollen submandibular gland. Which of the following bacterial pathogens is most frequently isolated in this condition?
qs.e: Bacterial sialadenitis most often involves the major salivary glands, particularly the submandibular glands, with Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus viridans being the most frequent pathogens. Paramyxovirus causes viral sialadenitis (mumps), not bacterial infections.
